en: I salute him who bears the weight of a mass of matted locks upon his head, who feeds on poison, who is the destroyer of all, who sports on Mount Kailāsa, and who is the further shore of the ocean of existence. 1.
I salute him whose forehead shines with the digit of the moon, who has a serpent around his neck, and who is the protector of the three worlds.

I bow to Kāla, who wears a garland of human heads, who is both time and tender toward time. (2) I bow to the Dark One, the cause [of all], who has destroyed Kāma with a wrathful glance, who delights in his own Self, whose garment is the king of serpents, and who brings an end to the sorrow of worldly existence. (3)

I bow to Him who bears upon His waist the serpent that sports there, who has abandoned all sacrificial rites, whose renunciation is most wonderful, who is free from passion for the flavors of sense-objects, and who assumes a portion in the sacrifices;
to Him who brought an end to the demons beginning with Tripura, the beloved of Girijā, who is eternally tranquil.
I bow to the Lord of the hosts of gods, whose hair is bathed in the celestial river, who has subdued Death through his divine play, who shines within the hearts of embodied beings,
who is free from the affliction of worldly existence, and who is the abode of all desired perfections. (6)

I worship Him who holds the Pināka bow in His palm, who is free from old age, who is the ripening of good deeds, who has surpassed the path of others, who is beyond the reach of the wretched, and who is saluted by hosts of gods.
I worship Him whose form is adorned with ashes, who is difficult to overcome through illusion, and who has abandoned all calamity.

I salute him, who is accompanied by the host of Pramathas, incessantly, morning and evening. He who, with a concentrated mind, constantly recites these eight verses composed by Brahmānanda, attains at the end the very state of Śiva.
Thus ends the Śrīśaṅkarāṣṭaka composed by the illustrious Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmananda.
